title: Import resources and reconcile drift
scenario:
Your organization is moving the `orders` application to Terraform. Before the move, the operations team launched the EC2 instance `legacy-api`, its security group `legacy-api-sg` and the IAM role `legacy-api-role` in the AWS console. The configuration in `/home/coder/lab` already manages the application's S3 buckets and has been applied. Since the last apply, someone has also changed the buckets in the console.

The configuration is initialized. The `aws` CLI is configured for the account and region `us-east-1`.

tasks.text:
Bring the IAM role `legacy-api-role` under Terraform management.

- The resource address must be `aws_iam_role.legacy_api`.
- Use an `import` block. The import ID of an IAM role is its name.
- Write a matching `resource` block yourself, then run `terraform apply`.

Hint: the [import block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) docs show an example. Copy the trust policy from `aws iam get-role --role-name legacy-api-role` and wrap it in `jsonencode()`.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform state list`. The output should include `aws_iam_role.legacy_api`, and `terraform plan` should report no changes for it.

tasks.text:
Bring the EC2 instance tagged `Name = legacy-api` under management as `aws_instance.legacy_api`.

- Look up the instance ID with `aws ec2 describe-instances`.
- Add an `import` block, then let Terraform write the resource block: `terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated.tf`.
- Review `generated.tf`: remove arguments that cause errors or conflicts, then apply.
- The instance must not be replaced.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan`. It should not show `aws_instance.legacy_api` at all.

tasks.text:
Someone changed the `Environment` tag of the bucket `orders-artifacts` to `dev` and added the tag `CostCenter = cc-4711`. Both changes were made outside Terraform.

- The `Environment` tag must be `prod` again.
- The `CostCenter` tag is approved: keep it in AWS and add it to the configuration.

Hint: `terraform plan -refresh-only` shows what changed in AWS.
tasks.validation: Run `aws s3api get-bucket-tagging --bucket orders-artifacts`. The output should show `Environment = prod` and `CostCenter = cc-4711`.
Run `terraform plan`. The output should end with `No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.`

tasks.text:
Import the EC2 instance tagged `Name = legacy-api` and the IAM role `legacy-api-role` into the configuration.

- Use `import` blocks.
- The resource addresses must be `aws_instance.legacy_api` and `aws_iam_role.legacy_api`.
- Neither resource may be modified or replaced.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan`. The plan should not propose any change to `aws_instance.legacy_api` or `aws_iam_role.legacy_api`.

tasks.text:
Import the security group `legacy-api-sg` as `aws_security_group.legacy_api`.

- Its existing ingress rule must remain unchanged.
- `aws_instance.legacy_api` must reference the security group through `aws_security_group.legacy_api.id` instead of a hard-coded ID.
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-names legacy-api-sg`. The HTTPS ingress rule should still exist, and `terraform plan` should report no changes for the security group.

tasks.text:
The tags of the bucket `orders-artifacts` were changed outside Terraform.

- The change to `Environment` was not approved. Restore the value from the configuration.
- The new tag `CostCenter` was approved. Keep it.
tasks.validation: Run `aws s3api get-bucket-tagging --bucket orders-artifacts`. The output should show `Environment = prod` and `CostCenter = cc-4711`.

tasks.text:
The analytics team takes over the bucket `orders-reports` and will manage it in its own configuration.

- Stop managing the bucket in this configuration.
- The bucket must not be deleted.
- Finish with a clean workspace.
tasks.validation: Run `aws s3api head-bucket --bucket orders-reports`, which should succeed. `terraform state list` should not include `aws_s3_bucket.reports`, and `terraform plan` should report no changes.

tasks.text:
Import the EC2 instance `legacy-api`, its security group `legacy-api-sg`, the IAM role `legacy-api-role` and the instance profile `legacy-api-profile`.

- Addresses: `aws_instance.legacy_api`, `aws_security_group.legacy_api`, `aws_iam_role.legacy_api`, `aws_iam_instance_profile.legacy_api`.
- The instance must reference the security group and the instance profile, and the instance profile must reference the role. No hard-coded IDs or names in those arguments.
- Nothing may be modified or replaced.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan`. The plan should report no changes for these four resources.

tasks.text:
Three worker instances, `legacy-worker-a`, `legacy-worker-b` and `legacy-worker-c`, were launched by hand.

- Manage them with a single `aws_instance.worker` resource that uses `for_each` with the keys `a`, `b` and `c`.
- Each worker must keep its instance ID.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform state list`. The output should include `aws_instance.worker["a"]`, `aws_instance.worker["b"]` and `aws_instance.worker["c"]`.

tasks.text:
Reconcile the bucket `orders-artifacts`.

- Restore the unapproved change to `Environment` and keep the approved tag `CostCenter`.
- Rename the resource to `aws_s3_bucket.build_artifacts` without recreating the bucket.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform state list`. The output should include `aws_s3_bucket.build_artifacts`, and `aws s3api get-bucket-tagging --bucket orders-artifacts` should show `Environment = prod` and `CostCenter = cc-4711`.

tasks.text: Hand the bucket `orders-reports` over to the analytics team. Stop managing it here without deleting it, and remove its configuration. Finish with a clean workspace.
tasks.validation: Run `aws s3api head-bucket --bucket orders-reports`, which should succeed, and `terraform plan` should report no changes.
